programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: Gerry is turning forty, and after finding a letter he wrote to himself ten years earlier, he becomes acutely aware of everything he has failed to accomplish. Clearly not the family man, Gerry attempts to prove that he’s the other type of “awesome forty.” But when his wild night out doesn’t go as planned, Gerry takes drastic measures to meet the expectations set out in his own letter. Meanwhile, Simon’s ferret goes missing and Lisa wants to impress the chairman of the board of trustees by putting on an elaborate fun fair in his honour, which quickly devolves into a complete disaster.

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: After waking up married and quite hung-over, Gerry and Lisa do their best to face the workday. They quickly realize, however, that this ‘accidental marriage’ thing is getting in the way and they set off to get an annulment as soon as possible. Meanwhile, Nisha accepts an invitation to have dinner with Simon and his mother in the hopes of mending fences. But when Angela’s date shows up, bearing an uncanny resemblance to Simon, it becomes clear that Angela’s acceptance of Nisha doesn’t come without strings. Ms. Terdie feels redundant when she learns that Robert has ordered e-readers for the students.

programme.title: Kim's Convenience
programme.desc: Kimchee’s excited to host a visit from his out-of-town mom. Jung looks forward to the reunion, but doesn’t realize the feeling might not be mutual. When Gerald asks Appa for a reference letter, Janet tries to salvage the situation without looking like a meddler. Appa makes an embarrassing spelling mistake on a store sign, causing Umma to take over sign duty. But Umma’s English might not be as good as she thinks.

programme.title: Kim's Convenience
programme.desc: Appa and Umma lie to get out of vacationing with their friends the Lees. But when the truth gets back to the Lees, Appa and Umma are determined to find the cause of the leak. Janet finally lands her first paid photography work. Unfortunately, it’s taking her ex-boyfriend’s engagement photos. Jung considers himself a master of impressions, but he soon finds it’s easier to dish it out than to take it.

programme.title: Kim's Convenience
programme.desc: When Umma gets rid of some of Janet’s things, Janet retaliates. Appa sympathizes with both sides of the dispute, but aims to work the situation to his advantage. Kimchee is on a mission to ask out his long-time crush, but has trouble navigating Jung and Shannon’s conflicting dating advice.

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: Gerry sees dollar signs when he learns that young Hayden’s father is sick, very rich, and planning to leave something to Hayden’s favourite staff members. Already established as Hayden’s Number One teacher, Gerry awaits his monetary gift with eager anticipation, only to discover that his ‘gift’ is legal guardianship of Hayden. But Gerry’s initial disappointment is quickly remedied by the financial contribution that accompanies said guardianship. Unfortunately, raising a child turns out to be a tad more expensive than Gerry had anticipated. Meanwhile, Robert becomes co-principal and takes every opportunity to ensure that all staff and students understand that he is no longer Lisa’s subordinate. Nisha jumps in on some innocent student games during recess, only to injure herself and ruin everything.

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: It’s almost March break and all of the staff members seem to have saved enough money for a vacation, except for Gerry. In a desperate effort to make some fast cash for a trip of his own, he decides to take a side job teaching in a prison. Gerry manages to establish a surprisingly positive rapport with the inmates, only to find himself the accidental drug mule for one of his new students. Meanwhile, Simon has been teaching an ESL class and becomes convinced one of his students has a much better grasp of the English language than he’s been letting on. Nisha has been tutoring students at their homes, but finds the work environments difficult to navigate.

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: After one of Gerry’s students skips a detention for a theatre rehearsal, Gerry confronts the student mid-rehearsal and unleashes a barrage of vitriol that impresses director Emma so much so that she immediately fires the student, offering Gerry the starring role instead. Will this be the birth of a brilliant thespian? In an effort to motivate her lazy students, Bobbi equips them all with heart monitors. At first, her efforts appear to be successful, but Bobbi soon finds herself unintentionally tracking a different type of student exercise. Nisha’s been having trouble getting her class to respect her authority, but has figured out that she can manipulate them into paying attention by crying in the classroom. Robert cracks down on Nisha’s unconventional tactic, only to find himself taking a page out of her book.

He sets out to do the only right thing: throw the first game, thereby freeing up his Saturday. programme.title: Kim's Convenience
programme.desc: Appa uses an old ping-pong table to try and relive his former glory, but the game soon threatens his already delicate relationship with Jung. Umma wants to spend more mother-daughter bonding time with Janet, but when Janet rejects her, Umma soon finds a replacement. A surprise gift basket brings workplace tension to Handy.

programme.title: Kim's Convenience
programme.desc: Appa and Umma discover an exciting new way to spice up their relationship, but Janet threatens to ruin their fun. Jung tries to help Kimchee prepare for his first corporate presentation as Handy’s assistant manager, but Kimchee insists on doing things his own way.

programme.title: Kim's Convenience
programme.desc: Kimchee’s excited to host a visit from his out-of-town mom. Jung looks forward to the reunion, but doesn’t realize the feeling might not be mutual. When Gerald asks Appa for a reference letter, Janet tries to salvage the situation without looking like a meddler. Appa makes an embarrassing spelling mistake on a store sign, causing Umma to take over sign duty. But Umma’s English might not be as good as she thinks.

programme.title: Kim's Convenience
programme.desc: Appa and Umma lie to get out of vacationing with their friends the Lees. But when the truth gets back to the Lees, Appa and Umma are determined to find the cause of the leak. Janet finally lands her first paid photography work. Unfortunately, it’s taking her ex-boyfriend’s engagement photos. Jung considers himself a master of impressions, but he soon finds it’s easier to dish it out than to take it.

programme.title: Kim's Convenience
programme.desc: When Umma gets rid of some of Janet’s things, Janet retaliates. Appa sympathizes with both sides of the dispute, but aims to work the situation to his advantage. Kimchee is on a mission to ask out his long-time crush, but has trouble navigating Jung and Shannon’s conflicting dating advice.

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: Gerry is turning forty, and after finding a letter he wrote to himself ten years earlier, he becomes acutely aware of everything he has failed to accomplish. Clearly not the family man, Gerry attempts to prove that he’s the other type of “awesome forty.” But when his wild night out doesn’t go as planned, Gerry takes drastic measures to meet the expectations set out in his own letter. Meanwhile, Simon’s ferret goes missing and Lisa wants to impress the chairman of the board of trustees by putting on an elaborate fun fair in his honour, which quickly devolves into a complete disaster.

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: After waking up married and quite hung-over, Gerry and Lisa do their best to face the workday. They quickly realize, however, that this ‘accidental marriage’ thing is getting in the way and they set off to get an annulment as soon as possible. Meanwhile, Nisha accepts an invitation to have dinner with Simon and his mother in the hopes of mending fences. But when Angela’s date shows up, bearing an uncanny resemblance to Simon, it becomes clear that Angela’s acceptance of Nisha doesn’t come without strings. Ms. Terdie feels redundant when she learns that Robert has ordered e-readers for the students.

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: As Gerry begins the process of moving in to Lisa’s apartment, Lisa finds herself deeply regretting her decision to give the marriage a shot. Meanwhile, in an effort to get in shape and lower his stress levels, Robert gets himself a treadmill desk. Trudy explains that Robert’s new attire combined with the full-body sweat and disturbing ‘workout’ noises emanating from his office are unprofessional and disruptive, but her words land on deaf ears. Bobbi takes great pride in learning that she has inspired a former student to become a singer/songwriter, but she soon realizes her pride might be misplaced.

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: Gerry sees dollar signs when he learns that young Hayden’s father is sick, very rich, and planning to leave something to Hayden’s favourite staff members. Already established as Hayden’s Number One teacher, Gerry awaits his monetary gift with eager anticipation, only to discover that his ‘gift’ is legal guardianship of Hayden. But Gerry’s initial disappointment is quickly remedied by the financial contribution that accompanies said guardianship. Unfortunately, raising a child turns out to be a tad more expensive than Gerry had anticipated. Meanwhile, Robert becomes co-principal and takes every opportunity to ensure that all staff and students understand that he is no longer Lisa’s subordinate. Nisha jumps in on some innocent student games during recess, only to injure herself and ruin everything.

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: It’s almost March break and all of the staff members seem to have saved enough money for a vacation, except for Gerry. In a desperate effort to make some fast cash for a trip of his own, he decides to take a side job teaching in a prison. Gerry manages to establish a surprisingly positive rapport with the inmates, only to find himself the accidental drug mule for one of his new students. Meanwhile, Simon has been teaching an ESL class and becomes convinced one of his students has a much better grasp of the English language than he’s been letting on. Nisha has been tutoring students at their homes, but finds the work environments difficult to navigate.

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: After one of Gerry’s students skips a detention for a theatre rehearsal, Gerry confronts the student mid-rehearsal and unleashes a barrage of vitriol that impresses director Emma so much so that she immediately fires the student, offering Gerry the starring role instead. Will this be the birth of a brilliant thespian? In an effort to motivate her lazy students, Bobbi equips them all with heart monitors. At first, her efforts appear to be successful, but Bobbi soon finds herself unintentionally tracking a different type of student exercise. Nisha’s been having trouble getting her class to respect her authority, but has figured out that she can manipulate them into paying attention by crying in the classroom. Robert cracks down on Nisha’s unconventional tactic, only to find himself taking a page out of her book.

Appa makes an embarrassing spelling mistake on a store sign, causing Umma to take over sign duty. But Umma’s English might not be as good as she thinks.

programme.title: Kim's Convenience
programme.desc: Appa and Umma lie to get out of vacationing with their friends the Lees. But when the truth gets back to the Lees, Appa and Umma are determined to find the cause of the leak. Janet finally lands her first paid photography work. Unfortunately, it’s taking her ex-boyfriend’s engagement photos. Jung considers himself a master of impressions, but he soon finds it’s easier to dish it out than to take it.

programme.title: Kim's Convenience
programme.desc: When Umma gets rid of some of Janet’s things, Janet retaliates. Appa sympathizes with both sides of the dispute, but aims to work the situation to his advantage. Kimchee is on a mission to ask out his long-time crush, but has trouble navigating Jung and Shannon’s conflicting dating advice.

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: Gerry is turning forty, and after finding a letter he wrote to himself ten years earlier, he becomes acutely aware of everything he has failed to accomplish. Clearly not the family man, Gerry attempts to prove that he’s the other type of “awesome forty.” But when his wild night out doesn’t go as planned, Gerry takes drastic measures to meet the expectations set out in his own letter. Meanwhile, Simon’s ferret goes missing and Lisa wants to impress the chairman of the board of trustees by putting on an elaborate fun fair in his honour, which quickly devolves into a complete disaster.

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: After waking up married and quite hung-over, Gerry and Lisa do their best to face the workday. They quickly realize, however, that this ‘accidental marriage’ thing is getting in the way and they set off to get an annulment as soon as possible. Meanwhile, Nisha accepts an invitation to have dinner with Simon and his mother in the hopes of mending fences. But when Angela’s date shows up, bearing an uncanny resemblance to Simon, it becomes clear that Angela’s acceptance of Nisha doesn’t come without strings. Ms. Terdie feels redundant when she learns that Robert has ordered e-readers for the students.

programme.title: Kim's Convenience
programme.desc: Umma is mistaken for a server at a school event for Janet. Appa takes up math tutoring to prove his teaching prowess. Shannon is finally single but will Jung make a move?

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: Gerry walks in on Trudy and Emma watching a viral video of a bus driver being bullied by students. After learning about a crowdfunding effort that raised money for the poor bus driver, he recruits Simon to help him stage a ‘bullying’ incident on the bus, in which he is to be the sad victim. Meanwhile, Bobbi takes a dozen pregnancy tests and finally accepts that she’s pregnant. When the tests are discovered, she finds herself roped into Robert’s misguided hunt for twelve frightened pregnant young students.. Dwyer has a new lady in his life and seems happier than he’s been in a long time. Nisha couldn’t be more pleased for him, until she discovers that his new love interest bears a striking resemblance to the sketch composite of the suspect in his late wife’s murder case.

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: It’s almost the end of the school year, and Gerry seems to be the only teacher at Xavier who hasn’t been offered a full-time contract for next fall. Even after Gerry plays the marriage card, it seems Lisa can’t guarantee him anything beyond fulltime substitute. Unwilling to accept this fate, Gerry gets an idea to start his own Charter school. Meanwhile, Robert and Bobbi interview applicants to fill Bobbi’s position while she’s away on maternity leave. Her initial concern about finding a qualified candidate is replaced with a deep insecurity that she won’t even be missed when the candidates prove quite overqualified. Lisa pulls out all the stops to throw an end-of-year faculty party. But when her efforts seem to go unappreciated, Lisa makes a bold move.

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: It’s a new school year and Gerry has finally achieved his goal: full-time Phys Ed! But when he finds out how Bobbi’s been teaching Phys Ed, Gerry’s appalled, and sets out to teach the course the way it should be taught…or the way he thinks it should be taught, anyways. Meanwhile, Dwyer learns the ropes to his newly appointed position of Vice Principal; and Nisha, fresh off her camp counsellor summer job, struggles to reset boundaries with three seniors.
programme.sub-title: Gerry Wants to Make Phys Ed Great Again

programme.title: Angie Gensler
programme.desc: News - Angie Gensler is a mother and personal trainer who was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2004. In this episode, Mathew Embry speaks with Angie about her diagnosis and why she ultimately chose not to pursue drug treatments. Instead, she focused on lifestyle changes including diet, exercise, and daily discipline. Her story is an inspiration to anyone navigating a difficult diagnosis.
